summary: Backend-only testing of the new /api/wearable/* endpoints (HBand vendor-agnostic layer). Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_wearable_api.py (16 pytest cases) covering device CRUD (create/list/re-pair/update/delete), measurement batch upsert + dedupe + query filters, sleep session batch + dedupe, sync-status append+list, daily-summary aggregation & completeness, and delete with/without purge_data. All 16 tests passed (100%). Unique user_ids ('e2e-wearable-<hex>') used for isolation; test devices are purged in the fixture teardown and via purge_data=true where relevant.
critical_code_review_comments: wearable.py delete_device without purge_data leaves orphaned measurements/sleep/sync_logs referencing a device_id that no longer exists. Consider documenting or auto-tagging orphans, or making purge default true.

MeasurementIn.measured_at is a free-form string (ISO-8601) — no server-side validation. Malformed timestamps will still be accepted and can break daily-summary aggregation. Consider validating with datetime parser or pydantic AwareDatetime.

daily_summary computes UTC-based day windows using string comparison on ISO-8601. Works because ISO strings are lexicographically ordered when zoned identically, but mixed timezones from the client would cause silent misplacement. Consider normalising measured_at to UTC on insert.

_ensure_indexes wraps all index creations in a single try/except and swallows exceptions — an index-conflict on one collection prevents the others from being (re)created. Consider per-collection try/except.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral user_ids of form 'e2e-wearable-<8hex>' with paired demo devices. All test data cleaned up automatically (purge_data=true) except the small residuals from test_delete_without_purge_keeps_measurements which are attached to a unique throwaway user_id and do not pollute real data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All /api/wearable endpoints green. If HBand real-device (EAS build) integration lands later, add a provider='hband' variant and dedupe test with duplicate ble_address across users. Frontend WearableProvider abstraction & 7-step onboarding still untested (explicitly out of scope this round).
